messages.content: Compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. Return JSON only. Use only what the text explicitly establishes. Do NOT invent an unmentioned release, retrieval, transfer, extra grip capacity, hidden hand position, or other transition. Treat one hand or foot as one exclusive physical resource for independent actions: if it is explicitly occupied and the next action needs that same hand/foot for a different independent task, that is CONFLICT unless the next text explicitly frees, transfers, repositions, or reuses the same held object for that action. COMPATIBLE = the next action follows physically from the established state. CONFLICT = the next action requires an occupied body part/object/state to be incompatible at the same time, or reverses an established state without an explicit transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text truly lacks enough physical information to decide. Do not rescue a contradiction by imagining a possible off-screen action.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Iris removes the right glove.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Iris later grips the valve with her bare right hand.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

We need to see if this next action follows physically from established state.

After removing the right glove, Iris's right hand is bare. So gripping a valve with bare right hand is compatible. There's no conflict because she has free right hand after removal.
